prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. TOBT=Target Off Block Time: issued only if capacity/ground path allow; frozen at horizon; revised only on turnaround-actor confirmation. Modes: Normal Operations; Adverse Weather Mode; Capacity Reduction State (Duty Manager declares); both allow binding metering; Recovery Phase; Contingency Fallback State (Airport Duty Manager declares after consulting Regional Flow Manager, Tower Supervisor, System Support Engineer; entry: auth loss, time misalignment, corrupted data, surveillance/flight-data mismatch, advisory delivery failure; exit: stable service, consistent data, user access, leads agree). Fallback: Portal down→Digital Briefing Room. DPS/CAM unreliable→RFM uses last verified Airport Capacity Plan with Airspace Sector Planner, Meteorology Briefing Officer. SAE down→Slot Coordinator manual slots at Contingency Operations Console; keeps last valid CTT; revised CTT only after Tower Supervisor and Ramp Control Lead confirm; checks Crew Duty Extension Log; Airline Operations Coordinator, Aircraft Operator Representative acknowledge. TSM, Ramp Movement Board advisory unless SSE confirms; DMS MUST NOT overwrite times; Arrival Regulation Console display only. Before automation return, Slot Coordinator reconciles manual record with SAE, conflicts resolved in Collaborative Decision Log. After restoration PAW receives outage timeline, manual intervention record, recovery milestones for Post Operations Report. Passenger data: secondary, advisory only, never replaces capacity/safety, no CTT entitlement. Airline Operations Coordinator sends Passenger Misconnect Count; Airline Interface Adapter validates timeliness/flight/ownership; Data Governance Steward sets aggregation (no names/bookings/itineraries); DPS estimates departure sensitivity; SAE keeps sequencing policy, runway/airspace, Ground Delay Program as controlling; tie-breaker only if Business Rules Registry permits per state; DMS recommends hold/release/resequence only within runway/surface envelope; Tower Supervisor may reject; Ramp Control Lead checks via Ramp Movement Board; ADM views recovery actions on Portal. Elements: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone; AAR=Airport Acceptance Rate); Capacity Assessment Module; Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time); Departure Metering Service (Emberline); North/South Runway Meters; Surface Surveillance Adapter; East/West Apron Sensors; Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove); Identity Access Service; Collaborative Decision Log; Tower

New part:
S752: The system records these actions as operational context rather than as passenger service tasks assigned to the airport flow management process.
S753: The Regional Flow Manager may consider a recovery action credible only when it is aligned with a valid Target Off Block Time, crew availability status, and confirmed aircraft readiness.
S754: If an airline indicates a recovery plan that depends on unrealistic turnaround timing, the Demand Prediction Service discounts the associated connection benefit.
S755: During Adverse Weather Mode, passenger disruption indicators are normally given less influence because the Capacity Assessment Module and Sector Load Monitor have reduced flexibility to absorb discretionary changes.
S756: During Recovery Phase, the same indicators can have greater practical value because metering margins may exist after the primary capacity constraint has begun to clear.
S757: The Arrival Regulation Console may show inbound connection pressure as context for arrival rate discussions, but it does not convert passenger handling needs into a separate arrival priority scheme.
S758: The Common Situation Display presents passenger disruption cues with clear labeling so that participants understand they are decision-support indicators, not commands.
S759: Every accepted use of connection-risk information in a metering decision is recorded in the Collaborative Decision Log with the responsible actor, rationale, and affected flight interval.
S760: The Performance Analytics Warehouse compares later delay outcomes with the logged rationale to determine whether the advisory use of passenger disruption data improved recovery performance.
S761: This approach keeps the primary system function focused on safe, efficient, and transparent traffic flow management while still allowing airline recovery information to inform proportionate metering choices.
S762: Cybersecurity for the Regional Flow Platform is based on centrally managed identities, explicit authorization, and traceable operational actions.
S763: The Identity Access Service is the authoritative source for user accounts, service accounts, role memberships, authentication policies, and session lifecycle controls.
S764: Each named operational user shall authenticate with an individually assigned identity before accessing the Airport CDM Portal, Digital Briefing Room, or any operational console.
S765: Shared operational accounts are not permitted for routine use because they prevent reliable attribution during time-critical flow management decisions.
S766: The Regional Flow Manager, Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, Slot Coordinator, and Airline Operations Coordinator receive role profiles that reflect their normal operational responsibilities.
S767: Role profiles shall grant the minimum access needed to view, propose, approve, or administer operational data within the Regional Flow Platform.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
